The New Zealand bowlers, relentless in their pursuit, claimed seven wickets since the morning session, with Ajaz Patel standing out as the pick of the bunch, securing four crucial dismissals. The Bangladesh second innings in this gripping Test match has concluded, with the team amassing a substantial total of 338. Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto demonstrated exceptional leadership with a brilliant century, setting the tone for the innings. Mushfiqur Rahim played a crucial supporting role, securing a well-deserved half-century, while Mehidy Hasan's resilient effort, particularly with the tail, saw him contribute 50 runs. This fantastic performance has granted Bangladesh a commanding second-innings lead of 331 runs, putting them in a formidable position.

Bangladesh, on the other hand, would have liked to bowl the Kiwis out much quicker but that wasn't the case. However, the lead was not that significant, so the hosts surpassed it very quickly. The openers, Zakir Hasan and Mahmudul Hasan Joy were a bit too defensive this time around. The former once again became a victim of Ajaz Patel while the latter was unfortunate to get run out at the non-striker's end. Najmul Hossain Shanto and Mominul Haque steadied their ship in this second session and added 90 runs together before a huge mix-up in the middle cost the latter his wicket after Tea. Shanto registered an excellent half-century and Mushfiqur Rahim used his experience well as they used the sweeps and reverse-sweeps brilliantly to counter the Kiwi spinners. Shanto went onto secure an exceptional hundred and became the first Bangladeshi player to score a century on captaincy debut and also the quickest to 5 Test hundreds for Bangladesh. He remained unbeaten on 104 while Rahim also made 43 runs and both of them will look to extend their already good lead even further on Day 4.

New Zealand started Day 3 well with Tim Southee and Kyle Jamieson adding important runs which helped them to take a 7-run lead at the end of their first innings. After that they came out to bowl and looked good but couldn't manage to make any inroads before Lunch. However, right at the start of the second session, Ajaz Patel got them their first breakthrough while Southee showed good reflexes to enforce a run-out. They couldn't build on it and allowed the hosts to build up a big partnership in the middle. There were some half-chances here and there but none fell in the way of the Kiwis until a huge miscommunication between the batters gifted them their wicket. The spinners did get some purchase on the wicket but some inconsistent lines and lengths allowed the Bangladeshi batters to settle in again and they were completely outplayed by the Bangladeshi skipper and Mushfiqur Rahim in the last session as they surrendered a big lead to the hosts.

Bad light has again forced Stumps here! Session Summary - 101 runs and 1 wicket in 30 overs. Day 3 is called a 'Moving Day' and this Test has moved towards Bangladesh as they are slightly ahead in the game with a healthy lead of 205 runs courtesy of some resilient batting performances, especially from their skipper, Najmul Hossain Shanto who has led from the front with a splendid century. New Zealand tried their best but it just didn't happen for them, but there is still a lot of time left in this game and we know that anything can happen in cricket.
